**Rename-similarity index: what reproduces on brain's 2091 records**

**What**: Re-measured git's rename-similarity index for an id-swapped `.memory/records/` record, on brain's own 2091 records with git 2.51.0. The docblock claim "a 60-record uniform random sample spanned R095–R098" does NOT reproduce. Five seeded mulberry32 60-draws (seeds 12345 / 777 / 20260816 / 4242 / 1) gave R090–R099, R091–R099, R091–R099, R092–R099, R091–R099 — every one reaching R099.

**Why**: Third review round on one sentence. It was a property of ONE draw stated as a property of the population.

**Where**: brain/scripts/memory/staged-records-check.mjs (parseStagedDiff docblock)

**Learned**: Facts that DO reproduce and must be kept: n=2091, min 671 B pairing at exactly R090, p25 = 2121 B, max 20532 B, 11.0% of records ≥6400 B, R099 above ~6.5 KB (measured 6090 B → R098, 7376 B → R099), and strict monotonicity of the index with record size (a 40-sample stratified redraw ordered with zero inversions). Since all ≥6400 B records pair at R099, P(a 60-draw contains no R099) = 0.890^60 ≈ 9.2e-4 — so any reported uniform span stopping at R098 is a ~1-in-1000 artifact, not a population property. Method: per sample, commit the record in a scratch repo, then delete it and write the id-swapped bytes at the new filename, `git add -A`, read the R-index from `git diff --cached --raw -z --no-abbrev`.
